;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2015–present)|Yemeni Civil War]], [[Saudi Arabian-led intervention in Yemen]]; [[Yemeni peace process]]
**The [[separatist]] [[Southern Transitional Council]] (STC) announces it is giving up its aspiration of self-rule in [[Yemen]] to implement a stalled peace deal brokered by [[Saudi Arabia]]. A spokesman for the group says they have "achieved their goal". The STC believes in establishing an independent state in southern Yemen similar to the [[South Yemen|one that existed between 1967 and 1990]]. [https://apnews.com/c0d8d226b7c8c655f34afe830d90c8c4 (AP)]
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**The U.S. imposes further sanctions on [[President of Syria|Syrian President]] [[Bashar al-Assad]] and his 19-year-old son Hafez, and warns that it will also sanction anyone who engages with the [[government of Syria|government]] in [[Damascus]]. [[Kelly Craft]], U.S. [[ambassador]] to the [[United Nations]], says the sanctions are not intended to harm civilians and that they do not target [[humanitarian aid]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mideast-crisis-syria-usa/u-s-slaps-sanctions-on-syria-in-push-for-assad-to-end-war-idUSKCN24U2F7?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Arts and culture
*Archeologists at [[Stonehenge]] pinpoint the origin of the structure's large [[Sarsen]] stones to a site {{convert|25|km|sp=us}} north near [[Marlborough, Wiltshire|Marlborough]], [[Wiltshire]], [[England]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-wiltshire-53580339 (BBC News)]

;Business and economy
*[[Cuba]] loosens some regulations on state-run companies and farmers, and allows for [[United States dollar|U.S. dollars]] to be used in internal trade, as the country seeks to revitalize [[Economy of Cuba|its economy]] in the midst of both the COVID-19 pandemic in the region and the [[Venezuelan crisis|economic decline]] of its [[Cuba–Venezuela relations|trading partner Venezuela]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-cuba-economy/cuba-loosens-straitjacket-on-private-sector-to-stimulate-economy-idUSKCN24U2UF?il=0 (Reuters)]
*The [[Central Bank of Brazil]] announces that it will start producing 200 [[Brazilian real|reais]] bills starting in August. [https://g1.globo.com/economia/noticia/2020/07/29/banco-central-anuncia-que-lancara-cedula-de-200-reais.ghtml (G1)]
*[[Zimbabwe]]'s [[Government of Zimbabwe|government]] signs a $3.5 billion agreement with the [[Commercial Farmers' Union]] to compensate [[White people in Zimbabwe|white]] farmers who were forcibly evicted from their land during a controversial land redistribution program in the [[2000s (decade)|2000s]] under former President [[Robert Mugabe]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/07/29/africa/zimbabwe-compensation-white-farmers/index.html (CNN)]

;Disasters and accidents 
*A train derails following a bridge collapse on [[Tempe Town Lake]] in [[Tempe, Arizona]], sparking a fire. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/amp/ncna1235191 (NBC News)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Iwate Prefecture|Iwate]] reports its first cases of COVID-19 infections, with two people testing positive. [https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20200729/p2a/00m/0na/026000c (''Mainichi Shimbun'')]
****Japan's daily new COVID-19 cases tops 1,000 for the first time. [https://www3.nhk.or.jp/nhkworld/en/news/20200729_41/ (NHK World)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]]; [[COVID-19 pandemic in Equatorial Guinea]]
****[[Vietnam]] repatriates 219 of its citizen from Equatorial Guinea with at least 120 of them reported to be COVID-19 infectees. [https://e.vnexpress.net/news/news/vietnam-flight-to-repatriate-120-covid-19-infectees-leaves-for-equatorial-guinea-4137297.html (VnExpress)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China]]
****[[China]] reports 101 new COVID-19 cases in the last 24 hours. This is the highest number of new cases since mid-April, and 89 of them are from [[Xinjiang]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-china-toll/china-reports-101-new-coronavirus-cases-for-july-28-vs-68-prior-day-idUSKCN24U00X (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
****The number of deaths in [[Brazil]] reaches past 90,000. [https://www.nst.com.my/world/world/2020/07/612664/brazil-covid-19-deaths-surpass-90000 (''New Straits Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Peru]]
****The number of cases in [[Peru]] reaches past 400,000. [https://dailyasianage.com/news/237044/peru-covid-19-cases-surpass-400000 (''The Asian Age'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Maryland]]
****[[Governor of Maryland|Maryland Governor]] [[Larry Hogan]] announces that the state will tighten their [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|mask]] mandate to prevent a spike in cases. [https://thehill.com/policy/healthcare/509681-maryland-tightens-mask-requirement-issues-travel-advisory-for-hot-spot (''The Hill'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Texas]]
****The number of cases in Texas surges past 400,000 as 313 COVID-related deaths are recorded in a day. [https://www.ft.com/content/57bab05d-3757-320f-ad1a-60316d5a4fee (''Financial Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Zimbabwe]]
***Incumbent [[Ministry of Agriculture (Zimbabwe)|Minister of Lands, Agriculture and Rural Resettlement]] [[Perrance Shiri]] dies from COVID-19 at the age of 65. [https://af.reuters.com/article/topNews/idAFKCN24U0UY-OZATP (Reuters)]

;International relations
*[[Fiji–United States relations]]
**[[Fiji]]'s opposition parties urge the government to reconsider its decision of closing Fiji's embassy in the [[United States]], the [[European Union]], and other countries, and blame [[China|Chinese]] influence in the Pacific. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/422305/fiji-urged-to-reconsider-closing-us-embassy (RNZ)]
*[[Belarus–Russia relations]]
**[[Belarus|Belarusian]] security forces arrest 32 members of the [[private military company]] [[Wagner Group]] at a sanitarium near [[Minsk]] in an overnight raid. All those detained are [[Russia]]n nationals, according to authorities. President [[Alexander Lukashenko]] convenes an emergency meeting with his security council, and instructs the Chairman of the [[State Security Committee of the Republic of Belarus|State Security Committee]] to ask Russia for an official explanation. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/jul/29/belarus-says-dozens-of-russians-arrested-ahead-of-presidential-election (''The Guardian'')]

;Law and crime
*[[George Floyd protests]]
**[[George Floyd protests in Minneapolis–Saint Paul]]
***A masked, umbrella-wielding man accused of helping incite riots and looting in the aftermath of the [[Killing of George Floyd|death]] of [[George Floyd]] is identified. [https://abcnews.go.com/US/man-helped-ignite-george-floyd-riots-identified-white/story?id=72051536 (ABC News)]
**[[George Floyd protests in Portland, Oregon]]
***[[Governor of Oregon|Oregon Governor]] [[Kate Brown]] announces that federal agents deployed to Portland, including all [[U.S. Customs and Border Protection|Customs and Border Protection]] and [[U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement|Immigration and Customs Enforcement]] officers, will start withdrawing tomorrow, per her conversation with [[Vice President of the United States|Vice President]] [[Mike Pence]]. [https://www.businessinsider.com/federal-agents-to-leave-portland-oregon-governor-kate-brown-2020-7?utm_source=notification&utm_medium=referral (''Business Insider'')]
**[[George Floyd protests in Wisconsin]]
***Two women, Kerida O’Reilly (33) and Samantha Hamer (26), are charged for attacking [[Wisconsin State Senate|Wisconsin State Senator]] [[Tim Carpenter]] outside the [[Wisconsin State Capitol]] building in [[Madison, Wisconsin|Madison]]. [https://thehill.com/blogs/blog-briefing-room/news/509678-two-women-arrested-in-beating-of-wisconsin-state-senator-at (''The Hill'')]
*[[Censorship in Turkey]]
**The [[Grand National Assembly of Turkey]] passes a new [[social media]] regulation bill that requires foreign sites to appoint Turkish-based representatives to help monitor content, and will punish companies that don't comply with fines and throttling bandwidth. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-security-socialmedia/turkey-passes-law-to-regulate-social-media-content-idUSKCN24U0EN?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Blasphemy in Pakistan]]
**A man accused of [[blasphemy]] under a new controversial law is shot dead by a gunman in the courtroom while he was standing trial for allegedly insulting [[Islam]]. The victim was part of the [[Ahmadiyya]] faith, a minority Islamic sect that [[Pakistan]] declared non-Muslim in 1974 for regarding [[Mirza Ghulam Ahmad|its founder]] as a [[prophet]]. The suspect was a former member. [https://www.dw.com/en/pakistan-man-accused-of-blasphemy-shot-dead-at-court-trial/a-54365714 (DW)]
*A man accused of attacking [[pro-democracy]] Hong Kong activist and convener of the [[Civil Human Rights Front]] [[Jimmy Sham]] says he was offered a [[HK$]]2 million bounty to "cripple" him in last year's attack. [https://www.scmp.com/news/hong-kong/law-and-crime/article/3095205/hk2-million-bounty-was-offered-cripple-hong-kong (''South China Morning Post'')]
*[[Morocco|Moroccan]] journalist and human rights activist [[Omar Radi]] is arrested and charged with rape and aiding foreign spies. The charges come after [[Amnesty International]] reported that the [[Government of Morocco|Moroccan government]] was using [[Israel]]i spyware to spy on dissidents like him. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-morocco-justice/morocco-arrests-dissident-journalist-on-rape-and-spy-charges-idUSKCN24U2V0?il=0 (Reuters)]
